t: The Ancestral Puebloans farmed the dry Colorado Plateau for some three thousand years, moving from caves and pithouses to villages of joined stone and adobe rooms called pueblos.
Between about 850 and 1150 they built the great houses of Chaco Canyon, linked by roads to dozens of outlying communities, and in the 13th century the cliff dwellings of Mesa Verde.
Drought and conflict led them to leave the Four Corners by about 1300 for the Rio Grande, Zuni, Acoma and Hopi country, where their descendants, the Pueblo peoples, still live.
dyk: Many Ancestral Puebloan buildings can be dated to the year their roof beams were felled: in 1929 a charred beam found at Show Low, Arizona, closed the gap in A. E. Douglass’s tree-ring record and gave the ruins exact dates.
ev: Maize farming begins on the Colorado Plateau in the Basketmaker II period
Basketmaker III villages take up pottery, the bow and arrow and beans
The great houses of Chaco Canyon, Pueblo Bonito among them, are built and linked by roads
Drought; Chaco’s power fades and Aztec on the Animas River becomes a leading centre
The cliff dwellings of Mesa Verde, Cliff Palace among them, are built and lived in
The Great Drought; by about 1300 the Four Corners region is empty as its people move south and east
The Coronado expedition storms the Zuni town of Hawikuh and reaches the Rio Grande pueblos
Juan de Oñate founds the Spanish colony of New Mexico

f.homeland: The Colorado Plateau around the Four Corners of the south-western United States, where Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado and Utah meet; later also the Rio Grande valley and the Zuni, Acoma and Hopi country
f.period: c. 1500 BCE–1600 CE: from the first maize farmers of the Basketmaker II period, whose beginning is debated, through Chaco Canyon (c. 850–1150) and the cliff dwellings of Mesa Verde (c. 1190–1285) to the founding of Spanish New Mexico in 1598; their descendants are the Pueblo peoples of today
f.known: Cliff dwellings such as Cliff Palace; the great houses and roads of Chaco Canyon, Pueblo Bonito the largest; kivas; black-on-white painted pottery and fine basketry; turquoise work; farming in a dry land
f.sources: Excavations and surveys at Chaco Canyon, Mesa Verde, Aztec, Canyon de Chelly, Betatakin and Keet Seel, Bandelier and Pecos; tree-ring dating, which fixes many buildings to the year; rock art and kiva murals; the chronicles of the Coronado expedition; the oral traditions of the Hopi, Zuni and other Pueblo peoples
